ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signers and material counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UK OFSI sanctions list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and Samoa FIU/domestic watchlists. PEP status is identified by role and jurisdiction; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, their family members and close associates. Beneficial owner identification applies to any natural person with at least 25% ownership or control, with uplift to 10% for higher-risk structures. Suspicious transaction reports are filed with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) — International Companies Registry; applications are submitted through SIFSA-licensed registered agents and there is no direct public electronic self-service portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Roman script and may be in English or Samoan; Samoan and English are the official languages. Chinese characters are not acceptable as the registered name. A Chinese trading name may be used only as a transliterated Roman-script alias in the constitutional documents, with a certified English translation of the Chinese-language memorandum and articles. The statutory suffix for an International Company is 'International Company' or the abbreviation 'IC'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the licensed registered agent must request the written grounds from SIFSA's International Companies Registry. A written appeal must be filed with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, annexing the proposed name, the SIFSA refusal letter, a statutory declaration of the grounds of appeal and any supporting trademark or consent evidence. The Registrar is to determine the appeal administratively within 30 days. A successful appeal results in a 30-day reservation. If the appeal is refused, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa within 3 months of the refusal. Extension of an existing reservation is not available; a fresh reservation may be filed after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or registered office is permissible for the statutory International Company, provided it is supplied by a SIFSA-licensed registered agent as the registered office address in Samoa. A PO Box alone is not acceptable. No physical office or local employees are required for the low-risk offshore TikTok Shop social commerce holding structure, but bank and payment-rail due diligence (TikTok Shop Payout and Wise B2B) will require a credible economic-substance explanation and a physical or operational address abroad for management and sales activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated at under 5% per annum for a passive non-resident-owned International Company with no Samoan bank account, no Samoan source income and no local employees. The likelihood increases to approximately 15–20% if the company opens a Samoan bank account, places a local director or maintains a physical Samoan office; unannounced inspections are most often directed at the registered agent rather than the company's virtual location.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; sections 6 (incorporation), 9 (memorandum and articles), 12 (registered office), and 26-29 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association and Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; subscriber shares may be issued without escrow; no capital contribution deposit required by the International Companies Act 1987
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the share subscription of the incorporator as set forth in the agreed capital schedule be and is hereby approved and the secretary shall issue the corresponding shares. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at the address maintained by the licensed registered agent, and such agent is authorized to receive legal process. FURTHER RESOLVED that the persons named to the Board in the Articles are appointed as the first directors, and the individual named by the Board as secretary and as principal officer are appointed. The directors are authorized to open bank accounts, engage payment service providers, and execute all ancillary documents to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) online name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Company name and three alternates via the SIFA e-filing portal. Pay the name search and reservation fee. If clear, the Registrar issues a preliminary name clearance valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English
Name reservation application form
Identity and address of incorporator
Proof of payment of name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a written appeal or submit an amended name with alternative wording; if objection is based on a conflicting name, request withdrawal and re-submission under a new distinctive name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association consistent with the approved name and authorized objectives. The incorporator executes the documents; signatures are notarized by a licensed notary public or witnessed by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of first director(s)
Consent of registered agent
Notarized identity documents of incorporator and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA objects to a provision, amend the Article by board or subscriber consent in a subjoined deed and resubmit within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, consent forms, and registered agent declaration at SIFA. Ensure all statutory fees are deposited in the approved government account and submit proof of payment with the physical or electronic filing.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 signed by registered agent
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act of registered agent
Statutory declaration of compliance
Government fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a query notice, correct the specified defect and resubmit within the correction period indicated; if the period lapses, pay a small reactivation fee and file fresh Form IC-1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The registered agent simultaneously registers the Company's registered office address at its licensed address and files the designated particulars of the registered office with SIFA.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by SIFA
Registered office address confirmation from agent
Filing of notice of registered office (Form IC-2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error, request rectification by returning the original certificate with a cover letter; alternatively, file a notice of change of registered office if the office address is not yet active.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) corporate registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, convene a written first board resolution or signed unanimous consent. File a notice of appointment of directors, secretary, and registered agent, and obtain the corporate records book and common seal (if desired).
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution or written consent
Consent to act of each director
Consent to act of secretary
Notice of appointment forms to SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed officer is disqualified, file a replacement consent and amended notice; no resubmission fee applies if submitted within 5 business days.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Independent State of Samoa - the single national tax and customs administration administering the Income Tax Act 2015, the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2011 (VAGST Act), the Customs Act 2014, and the Tax Administration Act 2012; official portal: www.revenue.gov.ws; customs declarations are processed on the ASYCUDA World platform. International Companies are incorporated by the Registrar of International Companies at the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); export-proceeds repatriation and exchange control are supervised by the Central Bank of Samoa (CBS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987: appoint a licensed resident agent, submit the memorandum and articles, name reservation, Samoan registered office, and director/shareholder particulars; no minimum capital is required, non-resident ownership is fully permitted, and the Certificate of Incorporation is issued by SIFA. Step 2 - Obtain the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN): file the MfR TIN registration application attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, charter documents, and identification of directors and beneficial owners; the TIN is a single reference used for VAGST, PAYE, customs, and tax correspondence. Step 3 - Customs registration: apply to the Customs Division (MfR) under the Customs Act 2014 for the importer/exporter code and ASYCUDA World access to lodge export declarations. Step 4 - VAGST registration: because zero-rated exports count as taxable supplies, the IC must register for VAGST once its actual or prospective 12-month taxable turnover exceeds WST 60,000; a newly formed exporting IC should register voluntarily at once to claim input VAGST credits on platform fees, logistics, and overheads; non-resident companies may register through the resident agent. Step 5 - Banking and exchange control: open a foreign-currency account with a licensed Samoan bank (the IC is deemed non-resident for Exchange Control Act 1975 purposes), receive TikTok Shop payouts, and maintain CBS records of export proceeds for repatriation within 180 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - the Samoan International Company is an entity-level limited-liability corporation placed in a statutory offshore exemption zone: under the International Companies Act 1987, as amended, the IC, its income, assets, securities, and transactions are exempt from all Samoan taxes and duties (income tax, capital gains tax, estate duty, stamp duty); the IC is deemed non-resident for exchange control purposes; it bears no Samoan income tax on global e-commerce profits; distributions to non-resident shareholders are free of Samoan withholding tax; for VAGST purposes the IC is a taxable person only if it carries on a taxable activity in Samoa, and its cross-border retail supplies are zero-rated exports. The classification is not pass-through; it is a corporate tax exemption zone, not a transparency regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Samoa; the IC's Tax_Exempt_Zone status is automatic under statute. Available statutory elections and choices: (i) conversion/re-registration as a domestic company under the Companies Act 2001, by special resolution filed with SIFA, which elects Entity_Level_Taxation and surrenders the offshore exemption; (ii) application for a licence to carry on domestic business with Samoan residents, which submits the IC to the Income Tax Act 2015 on Samoan-source income and to VAGST on local supplies; (iii) voluntary VAGST registration below the WST 60,000 threshold to recover input credits, with deregistration only by approval of the Commissioner once the taxable activity ceases; (iv) constitutional election of restricted or unrestricted IC status, which affects permitted activities and SIFA fees only; (v) no hybrid-mismatch election regime has been enacted - Samoa has not adopted the OECD/G20 hybrid mismatch rules, and the Commissioner's anti-avoidance powers are exercised under the Tax Administration Act 2012.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, acting as the monetary authority and the administrator of the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1977. All foreign exchange transactions in Samoa must be conducted through CBS-licensed authorized dealers (commercial banks). The CBS-operated national real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system is the exclusive settlement venue for domestic Samoan Tala (WST) transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed-float regime referenced against a weighted currency basket dominated by the NZD, AUD, USD, and EUR. Current-account convertibility for genuine trade in goods and services is generally accommodated through authorized dealers without ad hoc CBS licensing, subject to submission of standard supporting documentation (commercial invoice, transport documents, tax clearance, and a completed FX application form). Capital-account transactions — including inbound foreign direct investment, share subscription, shareholder loans, assignment of intellectual property, and any cross-border transfer of funds exceeding the regulatory reporting threshold — require advance CBS exchange-control approval; approvals are discretionary, typically require 1-3 weeks of review, and may impose conditions on the timing or amount of remittance. Dividend and profit remittance by a non-resident International Company is legally permitted, provided the company holds a valid tax-exemption certificate under the International Companies Act 2007, has filed its annual return with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), and presents a tax clearance certificate; however, in practice the remittance can be delayed by bank-level compliance review and is subject to a CBS declaration which can take up to 10 business days. WST is not deliverable or freely convertible offshore; there is no offshore WST interbank market, so any non-onshore hedge must be cash-settled in USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1977, a resident exporter must negotiate export proceeds through an authorized dealer in Samoa within three (3) months of the date of shipment and surrender 100% of the proceeds to a Samoan bank, converting them into WST at the prevailing authorized-dealer rate unless CBS grants a written exemption. For a Samoa International Company that is non-resident owned, does not carry on business with Samoan residents, and derives income exclusively from foreign commerce (including social-commerce sales through TikTok Shop), Section 187 of the International Companies Act 2007 disapplies these resident-based exchange-control obligations; consequently the IC is not statutorily required to surrender or convert TikTok Shop payout proceeds. Nevertheless, where the IC elects to maintain a Samoan bank account, the authorized dealer may still require: (i) a SIFA certificate of non-resident status, (ii) a declaration that no Samoan-resident business is being conducted, and (iii) a CBS Exchange Control form (EC-01) for any cumulative inbound remittance exceeding WST 1,000,000 (approximately USD 360,000) in a rolling 12-month period.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Wise B2B (Wise Europe SA / Wise US Inc.) is assessed as Low-Medium feasibility for the primary settlement rail. Wise does not support WST balances, does not maintain a Samoan regulatory passport, and cannot issue local WST account details; a Samoa-registered International Company may open a Wise Business account only if it can additionally evidence a registered address or permanent establishment in a Wise-supporting jurisdiction (e.g., New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, or the United States). The recommended architecture is: TikTok Shop USD payout (via Wise or direct SWIFT) to a Wise USD balance held by a supporting operating entity, followed by same-day SWIFT sweep to the Samoa IC's USD account at Samoa Commercial Bank; legally, the Wise account must not hold the Samoa IC's principal trade settlement balance because Wise is an e-money institution, not a licensed Samoan bank, and its regulatory status would create an unlicensed deposit-taking exposure under the Central Bank of Samoa Act. Other offshore digital EMIs (Payoneer, Airwallex, Dukascopy) are likewise not CBS-licensed; they may be used exclusively as collection convenience accounts with mandatory daily sweeps to the licensed bank, and any ATM/expense use in Samoa must be avoided to prevent the characterization of a Samoan place of business.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Act 2007 (as amended) and CBS KYC Guidelines require customer due diligence to be completed with a face-to-face interview of the directors or authorized signatories. ANZ Bank Samoa and BSP Samoa require at least one director to appear physically at the Apia branch and present original passports, original certificate of incorporation, and the SIFA-issued certificate of good standing; remote video KYC is currently not accepted for International Companies. Samoa Commercial Bank (SCB) permits a hybrid route whereby the UBO and director may execute a notarized account-opening resolution before a Samoan-registered lawyer or an overseas lawyer of a recognized jurisdiction, with the original certified pack and apostille couriered to Apia, followed by a mandatory video-conference with the SCB Compliance Officer; nevertheless, a single physical visit to Apia for two working days is the lowest-risk approach and substantially accelerates account migration, internet-banking token issuance, and correspondent-bank due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity due to the historical availability of bearer shares or nominee management in older International Companies; banks apply a full look-through for any natural person holding 10% or more.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Beneficial Ownership Register extract filed with SIFA within 14 days; (ii) notarized and apostilled corporate chart identifying all natural persons above the 10% threshold; (iii) passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), apostilled; (iv) a signed statutory declaration of UBO; (v) a banker's reference letter from the UBO's homebank (issued within the last 3 months); (vi) a professional CV or public business profile evidencing 5+ years of e-commerce experience; and (vii) a SIFA Certificate of Good Standing issued not older than 30 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume TikTok Shop retail revenue without obvious tax footprint; banks flag tax-evasion risk and require proof that the IC is genuinely tax-exempt and has no Samoan-source income.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) International Companies Act 2007 tax-exemption confirmation letter issued by SIFA; (ii) annual return confirmation for the most recent fiscal year; (iii) a board resolution declaring no Samoan-resident business and no Samoan-source income; (iv) a copy of the TikTok Seller Agreement naming the Samoa IC as the legal seller; (v) the latest three months of TikTok payout settlement statements; (vi) a compliance certificate from the licensed Samoan registered agent; and (vii) a written tax-clearance statement from a licensed Samoan tax advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound USD settlement flows from TikTok Shop triggering source-of-funds and trade-based money-laundering review for marketplace payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) TikTok Shop payout ledger or platform settlement report mapping the payout reference to the Samoa IC legal entity; (ii) customer order and fulfillment archive (buyer receipts, courier tracking, and logistics provider contracts); (iii) signed AML questionnaire completed by the IC's compliance officer; (iv) a conversion and fee reconciliation statement for any currency conversions; (v) explanation and evidence of prefunding of the settlement account; and (vi) a notarized undertaking to notify the bank of any transaction exceeding USD 50,000 or any change of business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound supplier remittances to China or Hong Kong, which create heightened sanctions-screening and trade-based laund-ering scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Commercial invoices and ERP inventory ledgers evidencing genuine merchandise purchases; (ii) supplier KYB pack (business registration, issued licenses, bank mandate, and beneficial-owner identification); (iii) transport documentation (airway bills, bills of lading, customs declarations, or last-mile courier logs); (iv) negative sanctions-screening confirmation for all UNSC, OFAC, and EU-list parties; (v) CBS Business Remittance Form / EC-01 as required by the bank; (vi) publicly accessible TikTok storefront or merchant URL corroborating the transaction; and (vii) a written compliance opinion from a licensed Samoan attorney confirming that the IC is not in breach of the Exchange Control Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: TikTok Shop payout rail: TikTok's settlement entity (typically TikTok Pte. Ltd., Singapore, or a US affiliate) initiates a SWIFT MT103 credit to the Samoa IC's USD account at Samoa Commercial Bank (or BSP), with the purpose of payment coded 'GOOD' (payment for goods), reference narrative 'Sales proceeds of online retail commerce - non-resident Samoa IC'; the MT103 narrative must expressly identify the IC's SIFA registration number so the beneficiary bank's CBS reporting is automatically satisfied. For shareholder or founder capital injection, route via SWIFT MT103 from the founder's corporate or trust account using purpose code 'GTRW' (transfer of own funds) with a board resolution authorizing the injection, a funds-availability certificate from the sending bank, and a funds-sweep instruction to keep the balance in USD; any inbound credit exceeding USD 100,000 equivalent must be pre-notified to the account relationship manager 48 hours in advance. WST conversion is permitted only for genuine local expenses (registered-agent fees, director travel, Samoan legal fees, and minimal administrative costs); monthly conversions above USD 20,000 equivalent require CBS form EC-01 and supporting invoices, and local payments must be annotated with the standardized purpose code '01100-Personal Remittances' or '09110-Corporate overhead' to avoid misclassification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments to China and Hong Kong: (i) standard SWIFT MT103 in USD via the Samoa IC's USD account, with beneficiary banks HSBC, Bank of China, or China Merchants Bank, using purpose code 'TRDS' (trade in goods) and the original commercial invoice as attachment; clearing typically completes in D+1. (ii) For CNY settlement, convert USD to CNH via a Hong Kong intermediary (using Samoa Commercial Bank's FX desk or a licensed HK money-services operator), then pay through CHATS with transaction code 2901 and the underlying invoice reference; the Samoa IC must maintain the audit trail from USD debit to CNH credit. (iii) Freight and fulfillment payments use MT103 purpose code 'FRFR' (freight) to the forwarder's USD or HKD account with the commercial invoice and packing list attached. (iv) For large purchase orders above USD 50,000, issue an at-sight commercial letter of credit via SCB or BSP using SWIFT MT700, advised by Standard Chartered or HSBC Guangzhou/Shenzhen, with 100% cash-margin cover prefunded to the issuing bank; the LC terms should require presentation of transport documents and a beneficiary certificate to prevent the application of Samoan exchange-control restrictions to the settlement. All outbound payments must be supported by the corresponding TikTok Shop order ledger to substantiate the trade nexus.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward (USD/WST) executed with an authorized commercial bank (ANZ, BSP, or SCB) under a short-form ISDA 2002 / Samoa-law confirmation, restricted to documented trade flows and requiring CBS acknowledgment for tenors above 12 months; cash settlement in WST is mandatory.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on WST/USD executed via a London or Singapore prime broker, cash-settled in USD, where the Samoa IC establishes a non-Samoan SPV to act as contracting counterparty; permissible only as a hedge of actual TikTok revenue exposure and prohibited for speculative positions.

USD/CNH cross-currency basis swap executed with the bank's treasury desk or a licensed HK intermediary to hedge the mismatch between USD-denominated TikTok revenue and CNY-denominated supplier costs, with 3-month rolling tenors and physical settlement through the Hong Kong CHATS corridor.

FX forward collar or participating forward for the USD/WST conversion budget, documented under an ISDA CSA with a zero-threshold margin arrangement; any notional above USD 500,000 requires prior CBS hedging approval under the Exchange Control Act.
USD interest rate swap to parallel-finance any settlement credit facility or overdraft at the Samoa bank; the instrument is USD-denominated and therefore outside WST exchange-control restrictions.

Vanilla FX swap (USD/AUD and USD/NZD) for Pacific-region logistics and warehousing costs, executed with the onshore bank's treasury desk under the trade-related 'investment purpose' exemption, capped at the projected 12-month logistics expenditure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (confirming company name, registration number, registered office, registered agent, directors and shareholder register status) together with payment of the annual International Company Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa, submitted through the appointed licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on each annual anniversary of the date of incorporation; no fixed fiscal-year cutoff. The return and annual fee must be lodged by the anniversary date, with a 30-day administrative grace period during which late lodgement is accepted subject to a statutory surcharge.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A surcharge of 10% of the unpaid annual fee applies if payment is made within one month after the due date; continued non-payment exposes the company to a Registrar strike-off notice and eventual administrative dissolution from the International Companies Register; restoration requires settlement of all outstanding fees, penalties, and Registrar reinstatement charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (UBO register update filed with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa, submitted via the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Return on the incorporation anniversary; any transfer of shares or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change or within 14 days of the company becoming aware of the change, whichever is earlier.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate government filing fee is imposed; failure to file is an offence under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018, rendering each defaulting director and the registered agent liable to monetary penalties, and persistent non-compliance is treated by the Registrar as a compliance default that may trigger administrative strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a Samoa International Company. A statutory audit is mandatory only where the company's constitution or a shareholders' special resolution requires it, or where the company holds a sectoral licence (banking, insurance, or trust business) whose licensing conditions impose an audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No specific accounting standard is prescribed for International Companies under Samoan law; the statutory duty is to maintain accounting records sufficient to show and explain transactions and to enable true and fair financial statements to be prepared. IFRS is commonly adopted on a voluntary basis where an audit is mandated by the constitution or shareholders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain and record the identity, nationality, and extent of economic interest of every ultimate beneficial owner as at the Annual Return anniversary date. On any share transfer, the company must update the Register of Beneficial Owners immediately, file the change with the Registrar within the prescribed statutory window, and obtain reconfirmation from both the transferor and transferee of their resulting beneficial holdings.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 800 per annum for licensed registered agent and registered office services in Apia, Samoa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; voluntary certified audit, where mandated by constitution or shareholders, approximately USD 2,500 - 5,000 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2012; 0% statutory exemption for an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are wholly exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, and stamp duty, with a 20-year statutory guarantee against newly enacted Samoan taxes. The only annual cost is the government fee (USD 500); no turnover-based or economic-activity tax applies to a compliant IC.
